statement: 201 positive integers are written in a line such that both the first and the last are equal to \(19999\). Each of the remaining numbers is less than the average of its two neighbors, and the differences between each of those numbers and the average of its neighbors are all equal to the same positive integer. Find the second-to-last term of the line.

Given several numbers, one of them, \(a\), is chosen and replaced by the three numbers \(\tfrac{a}{3}, \tfrac{a}{3}, \tfrac{a}{3}\). This process is repeated on the new set of numbers, and so on. Originally, there are 1000 ones, and the process is applied several times. A number \(m\) is called good if, no matter how many or what operations are performed, there are always at least \(m\) numbers that are the same. Find the largest possible good number.

Two circles of radius 1 that do not intersect, \(c_1\) and \(c_2\), are placed inside an angle with vertex \(O\). Circle \(c_1\) is tangent to one ray of the angle, and \(c_2\) is tangent to the other ray. One of the two common internal tangents of \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) passes through \(O\), and the other intersects the rays of the angle at points \(A\) and \(B\) with \(AO = BO\). Find the distance from point \(A\) to line \(OB\).

Consider the following 50-term sums:
\[S = \frac{1}{1 \cdot 2} + \frac{1}{3 \cdot 4} + \cdots + \frac{1}{99 \cdot 100},\]
\[T = \frac{1}{51 \cdot 100} + \frac{1}{52 \cdot 99} + \cdots + \frac{1}{99 \cdot 52} + \frac{1}{100 \cdot 51}.\]
Express \(\dfrac{S}{T}\) as an irreducible fraction.
An integer \(n \geq 3\) is called special if it does not divide \((n-1)!\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{n-1}\right)\). Find all special numbers \(n\) with \(10 \leq n \leq 100\).

Determine whether there exist positive integers \(a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_k\) such that all pairwise sums \(a_i + a_j\) (\(1 \leq i < j \leq k\)) are distinct, and among those sums there are 1000 consecutive integers.
